findings.issue: explicitWeakness detection only used the configured subject pronoun; object/possessive forms ('Zir weakness is Rust', 'Hir struggles with Rust') scored GOOD under a NEGATIVE_ASSESSMENT contract.
findings.reproduction: scoreCase NEGATIVE_ASSESSMENT with pronouns 'ze/zir/hir': 'Ze is weak at Rust.' OVERCLAIM after first fix; 'Zir weakness is Rust.' and 'Hir struggles with Rust.' returned GOOD.
findings.fix: naAllForms now covers subject/object/possessive and feeds both the subject alternation and the possessive ('X weakness is') alternation alongside his/her/their.

findings.issue: Named-subject is_type pattern captured a configured pronoun ('Hir is a nurse' -> subject 'hir'), emitting an unknown-entity claim that bypassed subject grounding.
findings.reproduction: extractClaims('Hir is a nurse at the clinic.', graph) produced {subject:'Hir',relation:'is_type',object:'nurse'}.
findings.fix: is_type subject canonicalization recognizes configured pronoun forms and emits subject='subject'.

findings.issue: Epistemic 'cannot confirm whether' phrasing parsed as DENY by the named-denial stance patterns, so bounded uncertainty was validated as a definitive denial.
findings.reproduction: parseLeadingStance('Morgan cannot confirm whether Rust is documented.') -> DENY; 'Morgan cannot use Rust.' -> DENY (correct).
findings.fix: Epistemic cannot-confirm/whether wording is classified QUALIFY before the named-denial patterns fire; definitive capability denial still DENY.

findings.issue: professional_inflation pattern dropped 'his'/'her' coverage and did not include configured possessives, so 'Ze developed zir projects professionally' escaped the inflation check.
findings.reproduction: validateAnswer('Ze developed zir projects professionally.', ...) reasons contained no professional_inflation flag.
findings.fix: Pattern rebuilt inside validateAnswer from getSubjectPronouns(knowledge): subject/object/possessive + his/her/their + 'the' all covered.

findings.issue: Pronoun-headed 'X is a <type>' claims escaped fabricated_occupation: headIsSubject (explicitRole path) lacked configured pronouns and the bare is-a subjectPattern required the literal first name.
findings.reproduction: validateAnswer('Ze is a support ticketing platform.', ...) valid:true, reasons:[] while 'Morgan is a support ticketing platform.' flagged fabricated_occupation.
findings.fix: subjectHeadRefs includes configured subject/object/possessive; bare is-a subjectPattern alternation includes configured pronoun forms (plus are/were).
